facts.statement: Liaoxipterus is a pterodactyloid pterosaur found in the Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Liaoxipterus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Barremian-Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The genus name Liaoxipterus combines the discovery locality Liaoxi with the Greek word for wing.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the discovery locality Liaoxi and a Latinised Greek pteron, "wing".

facts.statement: The species name brachyognathus means "short jaw" in Greek.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Greek brachys, "short" and gnathos, "jaw".

facts.statement: The type specimen is a 161-millimetre-long crushed mandible with only eleven short teeth on each side.
facts.quote: The genus is based on holotype CAR-0018, an almost complete but crushed 161 millimetres long mandible (fused lower jaws), which differs from that of all known other ctenochasmatids in its short teeth and low tooth count (eleven per side).

facts.statement: Liaoxipterus possessed a rounded jaw top filled with small, peg-like teeth.
facts.quote: The jaw of Liaoxipterus had a rounded top filled with small, peg-like teeth.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Liaoxipterus was an insect eater that may have been able to protrude its tongue like a chameleon to catch prey.
facts.quote: The shape of the teeth, and the anatomy of the hyoid (a bone that anchors the tongue muscles), suggest that it was an insect eater, and may even have had the capability to protrude its tongue in a manner similar to chameleons in order to catch insects.

facts.statement: Wang and colleagues suggested in 2006 and 2008 that Liaoxipterus belonged to the family Istiodactylidae, a view accepted by Lü in 2015.
facts.quote: Wang and colleagues suggested in 2006 and 2008 that it was actually an istiodactylid instead, an opinion that was accepted by Lü in 2015.

facts.statement: Liaoxipterus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: A 2012 analysis by Mark Witton found that Liaoxipterus and Nurhachius were not identical and did not group together in a phylogenetic tree.
rejected.quote: However, a 2012 analysis by Mark Witton found that these two istiodactylids were not identical and, more importantly, did not group together in a phylogenetic tree.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'did not group together in a phylogenetic tree'

rejected.statement: Recent analyses place Liaoxipterus as the sister taxon of Istiodactylus within the family Istiodactylidae.
rejected.quote: In the analyses, they recovered Liaoxipterus as the sister taxon of Istiodactylus within the family Istiodactylidae, and placed within the more inclusive group Istiodactyliformes.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the sister taxon of Istiodactylus within the family'
